### **Job Description and Duties**

The Inland Deserts Fisheries South Program is looking for a highly motivated Environmental Scientist to work with a dedicated team of fisheries professionals to address environmental stressors and drought resiliency for native fishes and other aquatic species.
  
  
Under the close supervision of a Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist is responsible for coordinating and implementing monitoring of environmental stressors for fisheries, native fishes, and other aquatic species. The incumbent conducts aquatic species stressor monitoring and rescues throughout the region. The incumbent closely coordinates with Fisheries Branch, other regions and Department functions, as well as other affected and involved local, State, and Federal agencies. The position coordinates field work activities, collects and organizes data, and prepares draft reports and correspondence for Department Leadership and partner State and Federal agencies.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement.

During this 12-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Ability to conduct biological resource work in the field over 45% travel throughout the state; and work at odd or irregular hours. Ability to use a personal computer and keyboard at least several hours a day, sitting most of the time, which involve walking or standing for brief periods to access files, references, and other program materials. Attend meetings and internal and external training. In addition to working with Regional staff, interact with headquarters staff and members of the public via e-mail, telephone and through virtual meetings. Possession of valid CA driver’s license. Ability to drive for up to 8 hours. Ability to work outdoors for up to week-long trips in variable weather conditions (32F - 120F), operate 4WD vehicles, wade in streams, and walk over uneven outdoor terrain carrying a 40 lb. backpack for up to 6 hours. As a condition of employment, the incumbent is required to wear an appropriate uniform consistent with CDFW’s Operations Manual (Section 12901) for various work situations, including field surveys and public interaction. This position offers the possibility of an office-centered telework agreement based on the Department's current Telework Policy.

Department of Fish and Wildlife

JC-537837



Environmental Scientist, Wildlife Biologist
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/17/2026**

**Application Methods:**

Electronic (Using your CalCareer Account)

By Mail

Drop-off

Print Job

Save Job

### **Job Description and Duties**

The incumbent supports comprehensive habitat management and wildlife conservation activities on the Grizzly Island Wildlife Area (GIWA). Duties include conducting wildlife surveys to assess species inventory, status, habitat use, production, population trends, and distribution. The position monitors wildlife populations associated with federal and State requirements, including the Federal Assistance (Pittman-Robertson) grant and listed species obligations. The incumbent coordinates with agencies, conservation groups, private landowners, and researchers to access lands and complete resource assessments, providing written reports to guide management actions.

  

Wildlife habitat management: The incumbent assists with mowing, noxious weed control, species eradication efforts, and the operation of water delivery systems to apply water for flood and irrigation cycles that support wetland habitat and benefit target wildlife species. The position provides biological expertise and best management practices for Suisun Marsh projects related to wildlife, vegetation, water, and threatened and endangered species. The incumbent develops geographic information system (GIS)/global positioning system (GPS) maps for habitat projects, vegetation, invasive species, public uses, and maintains digital resource data for the wildlife area. The role includes leading the creation and updating of Land Management Plans and representing CDFW in meetings related to land use, project development, and resource issues.

Hunting recreation: Includes coordinating regulations, guidelines, and hunter quotas; conducting elk hunter orientations and hunts; collecting biological samples from harvested game, assisting the Game Bird Heritage and Waterfowl Program with special hunt opportunities such as Junior Pheasant hunts; supporting waterfowl check station operations. The incumbent works closely with CDFW staff, volunteer land stewards, and hunters to ensure safe, equitable, and high quality hunting experiences.

The position represents CDFW policies and communicates wildlife management information to partner agencies including Suisun Resource Conservation District (SRCD), Department of Water Resources (DWR), San Francisco Bay Conservation and Development Commision (BCDC), United States Geological Survey (USGS), federal partners, private landowners, and Suisun Marsh Habitat Management, Preservation, and Restoration Plan (Suisun Marsh Plan; SMP) participants. The incumbent helps identify habitat projects and funding opportunities and collaborates with agencies on marsh wide resource issues.

  

ADDITIONAL APPLICATION FILING INSTRUCTIONS

Application packages (i.e., STD. 678, resume, and Statement of Qualifications) will be screened for writing quality, including spelling, grammar, and punctuation.

Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

  

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in-person at least four (4) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N-22-25. Additional in-office days may be required based on operational needs.

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

Involves regularly working outside in inclement weather and harsh conditions. Areas include uneven terrain in various environments. Requires ability to operate and drive numerous types of field equipment, boats, kayaks, all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), and 4x4 vehicles; use herbicides and application equipment; and use a computer and keyboard several hours a day. Complete field work as needed to evaluate wetland habitat and wildlife. Requires tolerating ticks and mosquitos. Routine work involves unusual hours and regular scheduling on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays during hunting seasons, requiring the ability to change hours of work due to wildlife area activities.

Special Requirements: Requires physical strength and agility; ability to swim 50 yards and stay afloat for at least five minutes; and the ability to lift forty (40) pounds. Requires the possession of a valid driver's license and ability to operate a state vehicle with four-wheel drive (4WD) on CDFW lands. Requires the ability to operate tractors, mowers, kayaks, John boat, or Whaler, and all-terrain vehicles (ATVs). This position may require a pesticide Qualified Applicator Certification (QAC) within one year of hire. Wearing a Department of Fish and Wildlife uniform is required as a condition of employment while conducting field work and public work duties. The employee is required to live in State-owned housing at GIWA based on the availability of move-in ready units at the time of hire, or as soon as a unit becomes available.

The designated headquarters location of this position is the Grizzly Island Wildlife Area Complex in Suisun City, California.

### **Job Description and Duties**

Under general supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist will conduct analyses, gather scientific data, review and report on pesticides and other chemicals that affect the environment and the food supply. The incumbent is responsible for providing depositions and analytical expertise on disputed analytical results. As an employee of the California Department of Food & Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. ### **Working Conditions**

The duties of this job are performed indoors approximately 100% of the time. The employee’s workplace has the necessary laboratory equipment and supplies for performing required analyses. The employee may be exposed to fumes, gases, or odors in certain work areas.

### **Department Information**

The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.

  

The Center for Analytical Chemistry (CAC) provides analytical expertise in environmental, food, and fertilizer safety, and in issues concerning crop protection, farm worker safety, data gathering activities, and emergency response. The Center is comprised of two main programs: Environmental Safety and Food Safety. The Environmental Safety laboratories (ESL) provide vital analytical support to the California Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) and California Environmental Protection Agency (CalEPA) by performing soil, water, and air analyses mandated by various environmental laws; monitoring pesticide exposure of field workers; and by performing regulatory testing of pesticides for label compliance. ESL also assists the Feed, Fertilizer, and Livestock Drugs Regulatory Services branch (FFLDRS) through the provision of label compliance testing of commercial fertilizers. The Food Safety laboratories (FSL) support DPR, US Department of Agriculture (USDA), and US Environmental Protection Agency (US-EPA) in their legislative tasks as well as the California County Agricultural Commissioners in their enforcement activities by conducting chemical analyses on environmental and food samples to monitor for and collect data on hazardous agrochemicals such as pesticides and their metabolites. The independent Quality Assurance (QA) section provides support to the CAC in the implementation and management of International Standards Organization (ISO) 17025 accreditation program, quality assurance of its testing activities, method reviews and validation and compliance audits.

**https://www.cdfa.ca.gov/is/cac/**

jobs.title: Air Quality Analyst
jobs.description:
Overview:

Kimley-Horn's Orange, CA office is seeking an Air Quality Professional with 5+ years of experience specializing in air quality permitting to join our environmental team. The successful candidates will assist in various projects, assisting industrial and municipal clients with their permitting, compliance, and planning needs.

Responsibilities:

* **Technical Support:**
  + Assist in conducting air quality impact assessments, analyses, and dispersion modeling.
  + Perform regulatory and technical analyses in support of permitting project in California and throughout the USA.
  + Familiar with modeling tools and software including CalEEMod, EMFAC, OFFROAD, CALINE4, AERMOD, CAL3QHCR, ISCST3, AERSCREEN, SCREEN3, and GIS.
* **Report Preparation:**
  + Prepare technical reports, environmental impact assessments, and documentation.
  + Conduct air quality impact analyses, health risk assessments, and greenhouse gas analyses.
  + Assist with the preparation of permit applications and compliance documentation.
* **Field Work:**
  + Participate in field studies and data collection activities related to air quality.
  + Participate in compliance audits for environmental topics including air pollutants, toxics, hazardous materials, etc.
* **Data Analysis:**
  + Perform emission calculations for various industrial processes.
  + Understanding design documents and engineering drawings.
  + Utilize Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and other relevant software for environmental analysis.

Qualifications:

* Degree (Bachelors or Masters) in Environmental Science, engineering (environmental, chemical, mechanical, civil), atmospheric sciences, physics, chemistry, data science or related field
* 5+ years of experience in environmental consulting, with a focus on air quality permitting
* Certified Permitting Professional (CPP) a plus
* Experience with data centers and power production
* Strong understanding of environmental laws, regulations, and standards (e.g., Clean Air Act, CEQA).
* Strong writing/verbal skills
* Working knowledge of GIS/ArcView
* Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal skills
* Positive attitude and a strong work ethic
* Strong sense of urgency and self-initiative to meet client deadlines
* Detail-oriented team player with an ability to contribute to a positive work environment
* Ability to work independently and as a team

**Salary Range**: $90,000 - $125,000

Why Kimley-Horn?:

At Kimley-Horn, we do things differently. People, clients, and employees are at the forefront of who we are. Clients know we prioritize achieving their goals and growing their success. Employees know our culture and approach to business are built on a desire to provide an environment for everyone to flourish. Our commitment to quality is only as good as the people behind it— that’s why we welcome and develop passionate, hardworking, and proactive employees. We take pride in how our employee retention, robust benefits package, and company values have led to Kimley-Horn’s placement on the Fortune “100 Best Companies to Work” list for 19 years!

*Key Benefits at Kimley-Horn*

* Exceptional Retirement Plan: 2-to1- company match on up to 4% of eligible compensation (salary + bonus) and additional profit-sharing contribution.
* Comprehensive Health Coverage: Low-cost medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
* Time Off: Personal leave, flexible scheduling, floating holidays, and half-day Fridays.
* Financial Wellness: Student loan matching in our 401(k), and performance-based bonuses.
* Professional Development: Tuition reimbursement and extensive internal training programs.
* Family-Friendly Benefits: New Parent Leave, family building benefits, and childcare resources.

### **Department Information**

The Mission of the California Department of Food and Agriculture (CDFA) is to safeguard a resilient food system and promote an equitable marketplace, cultivating a California grown food supply that is globally recognized for innovation, quality, and sustainability.

  

The Center for Analytical Chemistry (CAC) provides analytical expertise in environmental, food, and fertilizer safety, and in issues concerning crop protection, farm worker safety, data gathering activities, and emergency response. The Center is comprised of two main programs: Environmental Safety and Food Safety. The Environmental Safety laboratories (ESL) provide vital analytical support to the California Department of Pesticide Regulation (DPR) and California Environmental Protection Agency (CalEPA) by performing soil, water, and air analyses mandated by various environmental laws; monitoring pesticide exposure of field workers; and by performing regulatory testing of pesticides for label compliance. ESL also assists the Feed, Fertilizer, and Livestock Drugs Regulatory Services branch (FFLDRS) through the provision of label compliance testing of commercial fertilizers. The Food Safety laboratories (FSL) support DPR, US Department of Agriculture (USDA), and US Environmental Protection Agency (US-EPA) in their legislative tasks as well as the California County Agricultural Commissioners in their enforcement activities by conducting chemical analyses on environmental and food samples to monitor for and collect data on hazardous agrochemicals such as pesticides and their metabolites. The independent Quality Assurance (QA) section provides support to the CAC in the implementation and management of International Standards Organization (ISO) 17025 accreditation program, quality assurance of its testing activities, method reviews and validation and compliance audits.
